guitar.notes: Accurate: Paul Simon long associated with Martin and Guild acoustics.

tone.summary: A highly compressed, clean signal path using an OD pedal for warmth, followed by a low-gain US Deluxe amp model, paired with the US 2x12 cabinet and minimal room reverb to maintain a dry, natural folk ballad tone.
corrections: iconic recording is acoustic not electric

rig.name: Simon & Garfunkel - The Boxer - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up any background noise or hum inherent in the recording.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean recordings.

blocks.purpose: Mimic the natural compression of a professional recording setup and enhance fingerpicked clarity.
blocks.gap: None. Essential for achieving the sustained, even dynamics of folk ballads.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle lift and warmth to the signal without introducing noticeable grit or distortion.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used here as a clean tone enhancer, not for gain. A dedicated EQ might be better, but it serves the function of gentle signal reinforcement.

blocks.purpose: Bypass. No grit or crunch is desired for this dry folk tone.
Simulate the clean, articulate sound of a vintage American amplifier suitable for acoustic accompaniment.
blocks.gap: None. Ideal choice for clear, non-aggressive tones.

blocks.purpose: Provide a focused and articulate cabinet sound that complements the clean US Deluxe amp model.
blocks.gap: None. Matches the intended American folk tone.

blocks.purpose: Slightly scoop the low end and boost the upper mids/treble to enhance string clarity and definition.
Add a minimal, natural room ambience to give the signal depth without creating an artificial 'wash'.
blocks.gap: The reverb mix must be kept very low (20%) to avoid sounding like a wash.

improvements.summary: Replace the generic cabinet IR with a specialized acoustic/vintage speaker simulation for better string articulation.

proposals.reason: Enhance the natural, woody tone and clarity of acoustic strings.
